subject: math.SP
name: Spectral theorem for bounded self-adjoint operators
statement: Every bounded self-adjoint operator T on a complex Hilbert space has a unique projection-valued measure E on ℝ, supported in σ(T), such that T = ∫ λ dE(λ). This gives f(T) = ∫ f(λ) dE(λ) for bounded Borel functions f.

subject: math.SP
name: Spectral theorem for unbounded self-adjoint operators
statement: Every densely defined self-adjoint operator T has a unique projection-valued measure E on ℝ with T = ∫ λ dE(λ). Its domain consists exactly of the vectors x for which ∫ λ² d⟨E(λ)x,x⟩ is finite.

subject: math.SP
name: Compact self-adjoint spectral theorem
statement: A compact self-adjoint operator has an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors, with real eigenvalues. Every nonzero eigenvalue has finite multiplicity, and zero is the only possible accumulation point of the nonzero eigenvalues.

subject: math.SP
name: Holomorphic spectral mapping theorem
statement: If T is a bounded operator on a complex Banach space and f is holomorphic on a neighborhood of σ(T), then σ(f(T)) = f(σ(T)), with f(T) defined by the holomorphic functional calculus.

subject: math.SP
name: Gelfand spectral-radius formula
statement: For an element a of a complex unital Banach algebra, its spectral radius satisfies r(a) = limₙ→∞ ‖aⁿ‖¹/ⁿ = infₙ≥₁ ‖aⁿ‖¹/ⁿ.

subject: math.SP
name: Weyl criterion
statement: For a self-adjoint operator T and real λ, λ lies in σ(T) if and only if there are unit vectors xₙ in its domain with ‖(T−λ)xₙ‖ tending to zero. Moreover, λ lies in the essential spectrum if and only if such vectors can be chosen to converge weakly to zero.

subject: math.SP
name: Weyl essential-spectrum theorem
statement: If T is self-adjoint and K is a compact bounded self-adjoint operator, T+K on the domain of T has the same essential spectrum as T. Here the essential spectrum is the spectrum after removing isolated eigenvalues of finite multiplicity.

subject: math.SP
name: Variational min–max principle
statement: Let T be a lower-bounded self-adjoint operator with closed quadratic form q, and suppose it has at least k eigenvalues below the bottom of its essential spectrum. Its kth such eigenvalue, counted with multiplicity, equals inf over k-dimensional subspaces S of the form domain of sup over nonzero x in S of q(x)/‖x‖².

subject: math.SP
name: Courant–Fischer theorem
statement: For a Hermitian matrix A with increasingly ordered eigenvalues λ₁,…,λₙ, λₖ = min over subspaces S with dimension k of max over nonzero x in S of x*Ax/(x*x).

subject: math.SP
name: Kato–Rellich theorem
statement: Let T be self-adjoint and B symmetric with D(T) contained in D(B). If ‖Bx‖ ≤ a‖Tx‖ + b‖x‖ for x in D(T), with 0 ≤ a < 1 and b ≥ 0, then T+B is self-adjoint on D(T).

references.title: Kato: Perturbation Theory for Linear Operators

subject: math.SP
name: Friedrichs extension theorem
statement: Every densely defined symmetric operator that is bounded below has a self-adjoint extension with the same lower bound. The Friedrichs extension is the canonical extension associated with the closure of its quadratic form.

subject: math.SP
name: Stone theorem on unitary groups
statement: Every strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group U(t) on a Hilbert space has a unique self-adjoint generator A such that U(t) = eⁱᵗᴬ. Conversely, every self-adjoint A generates such a group.

references.title: Stone's theorem on one-parameter unitary groups — Wikipedia

subject: math.SP
name: First resolvent identity
statement: For a closed operator T and z,w in its resolvent set, define R(z) = (T−zI)⁻¹. Then R(z)−R(w) = (z−w)R(z)R(w), and the two resolvents commute.

subject: math.SP
name: Riesz spectral projection theorem
statement: For a bounded operator T on a complex Banach space and a positively oriented simple closed contour Γ in its resolvent set, P = (1/(2πi))∮Γ(zI−T)⁻¹ dz is a bounded projection commuting with T. Its range and kernel give invariant subspaces corresponding to the spectral parts inside and outside Γ.

subject: math.SP
name: Weyl eigenvalue asymptotic law
statement: For the Dirichlet Laplacian on a nonempty bounded smooth domain Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ, let N(λ) count eigenvalues at most λ, with multiplicity. Then N(λ) is asymptotic to |Ω|ωₙλⁿ/²/(2π)ⁿ as λ tends to infinity, where ωₙ is the volume of the unit ball.

subject: math.SP
name: Sturm oscillation theorem
statement: For the regular Sturm–Liouville problem −(py′)′ + qy = λwy on [a,b], assume p is positive C¹, q and w are real-valued continuous functions, w > 0, and the boundary conditions are separated and self-adjoint. Eigenvalues are simple and increasingly ordered; the kth eigenfunction has exactly k−1 zeros in (a,b).

subject: math.SP
name: Perron–Frobenius theorem for positive matrices
statement: A real matrix with all entries strictly positive has a positive spectral-radius eigenvalue that is algebraically simple, with strictly positive right and left eigenvectors. Every other eigenvalue has strictly smaller modulus.

subject: math.SP
name: Krein–Rutman theorem
statement: If T is a compact positive operator on a Banach lattice and r(T) > 0, then r(T) is an eigenvalue with a nonzero positive eigenvector.

subject: math.SP
name: Analytic perturbation theorem for simple eigenvalues
statement: Let T(z) be a norm-holomorphic family of bounded operators near z₀, and let λ₀ be an isolated eigenvalue of T(z₀) of algebraic multiplicity one. Near z₀, this eigenvalue and its rank-one Riesz projection depend holomorphically on z.

references.title: Kato: Perturbation Theory for Linear Operators

subject: math.SP
name: Birman–Schwinger principle
statement: Let V be a bounded nonnegative compactly supported function on ℝⁿ, H = −Δ−V on H²(ℝⁿ), and E > 0. Then −E is an eigenvalue of H if and only if 1 is an eigenvalue of V¹/²(−Δ+E)⁻¹V¹/², with the same multiplicity.
